key_insight: TrackEverything reframes video tracking as a 3D world problem instead of a frame-by-frame 2D problem, enabling dense tracking over long time horizons without the usual accuracy-versus-duration tradeoff. By using persistent 3D scene tracks, it can track many points continuously as videos get longer.
problem_solved: Most point tracking systems must choose between tracking a few points for a long time or tracking many points for a short time. This paper addresses the challenge of long-horizon dense tracking in videos.
method: Represents videos as persistent 3D scene tracks in world coordinates rather than only 2D image trajectories.
Uses de-duplication to avoid repeated representations of the same scene points over time.
Decouples tracking complexity from video length, making long-duration dense tracking more scalable.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could enable more robust video understanding in robotics, AR/VR, motion analysis, and scene reconstruction. It offers a practical path to tracking dense points across long videos without sacrificing coverage or scalability.

paper_title: TrackEverything: Long Horizon Dense Tracking via De-Duplicating 3D Scene Representations
